title: KENYA: “I saw his Potential,” Archbishop Emeritus says at Ordination of Kisumu’s New Auxiliary Bishop
desc:
Sr. Jecinter Antoinette Okoth, FSSA
When Archbishop Emeritus Zacchaeus Okoth was appointed Bishop of the then Kisumu Diocese on February 27, 1978, the newly ordained Auxiliary Bishop of Kisumu Archdiocese, Rt. Rev.  Vincent Ouma Odundo was just a few months from being born. 48 years later, in a moment that has left the faithful of Kisumu Archdiocese searching for words beyond coincidence, on Friday, February 27, 2026, Archbishop Emeritus joined the other Prelates to lay hands on Monsignor Odundo, who was ordained the third Auxiliary Bishop of Kisumu after the Servant of God Maurice Michael Cardinal Otunga who was the first Auxiliary Bishop and then the late Bishop Philip Sulumeti.
It is over 40 years today since I was appointed Bishop of Kisumu, said the Archbishop Emeritus in an interview with AMECEA Online, just after the ordination, his voice carrying the authority of a man who has shepherded a flock for decades, So I think it's God's plan and wish.
The story of Bishop Odundo and Archbishop Emeritus Okoth does not begin from the period the new Bishop was in the seminary. According to the Archbishop Emeritus, he knew the devout Catholic family of the auxiliary bishop, whose father served as Parish chairman some years back with the kind of dedication that left a mark on those who witnessed it.
I knew Vincent right from home, the Archbishop Emeritus recalled. His father was a dedicated Catholic who, at one time, was the Parish chairman. Since I lived in Nyabondo (The home parish of the Auxiliary Bishop) most of the time as a seminarian, I knew the family.
That seed of familiarity would grow slowly, steadily, across decades. When the newly ordained Prelate eventually presented himself for the priesthood, Archbishop Emeritus, by then a seasoned shepherd of souls, was watching closely. What he saw impressed him.
When I decided to ordain him, I had already seen his character. I saw his potential for the future. So, when he became a priest, I saw in him someone who could help in the growth of the Archdiocese, Archbishop Emeritus said.
It was Archbishop Okoth who then made a decisive call, sending the young priest to Rome to study Canon Law at the Pontifical Urbaniana University, a deliberate investment in a man he believed would one day help govern the Archdiocese. That calculation, it turns out, was more prophetic than even he may have imagined.
He added, We thank God for having chosen my young brother Vincent to be an Auxiliary Bishop.
For the People of God in Kisumu Archdiocese, Archbishop Emeritus said, I ask them to cooperate with Bishop Odundo, work closely with him and do their best as they continue the work of evangelization. I also urge them “to work alongside the new Bishop with diligence, strengthen their faith together, and to trust in the journey ahead.”
The symmetry of February 27 is the kind that makes the most rational mind pause. As the faithful gathered at Tumsifu Centre that Friday for the ordination of the Auxiliary Bishop, Archbishop Emeritus recalled his date of appointment as a Bishop on February 27, 1978, and the current Metropolitan Archbishop of the Archdiocese, Most Rev.  Maurice Muhatia Makumba, marked his 16th anniversary since he was ordained a Bishop on February 27, 2010.
Bishop Odundo has been serving as the Vicar of the Kisumu Archdiocese, working closely with Archbishop Muhatia.

title: KENYA: “I Come with a Message of Hope, Pray for Me,” Newly Ordained Auxiliary Bishop in Maiden Speech
desc:
Sr. Jecinter Antoinette Okoth, FSSA
Shortly after receiving the Episcopal ordination at Tumsifu Centre in Kenya’s Kisumu Archdiocese on Friday, February 27, Auxiliary Bishop Vincent Ouma Odundo asked the people of God for prayers and assured the congregation that he is ready to begin his ministry with a lot of hope.
In his maiden address, echoing the words from the Apostolic Nuncio's homily, which he expressed, moved him deeply and were quite inspirational, Bishop Odundo said, I am coming with the message of hope,” and also guaranteed the people of God his presence.
He reflected on the Nuncio's words: Semper vobiscum sum, meaning I am always with you, and assured Archbishop Maurice Muhatia Makumba, the Local Ordinary of Kisumu, of his service to the people.
Making his own personal pledge to the Metropolitan Archbishop, the Auxiliary Bishop said, Your Grace, Sono sempre con te, I will always be with you.
Bishop Odundo was equally clear about his role and said while addressing Archbishop Muhatia, My main role is to assist the Archbishop. I promise you my support, and I will do my best to also implement your mission and vision of the Archdiocese.
He reminded the faithful of the Archbishop's guiding motto: Duc in Altum, Latin for Into the Deep. He noted that this vision calls the Church to move beyond the shallows of comfortable faith into deeper commitment and action.
Your Grace, he said, “together with you, we will get to the depths of our faith and of what we do for the Archdiocese.
The newly ordained Bishop also used his maiden speech to thank all those who have supported him in various ways and attended the ordination event: Family members, Religious, clergy, the laity, politicians, especially his fellow priests, with whom they have journeyed together, and asked all to keep walking with him and praying for him.
